## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management tells has not changed in two years — the numbers underneath it have cracked. Across all four calls the message is identical and repeated almost word-for-word: scale toward "over 10,000 restaurants globally," drive average unit volumes (the average annual sales of a single restaurant, or "AUV") from ~$2 million toward "$3 million," and do it with an "asset-light, highly franchised model." The consumer was flagged as soft but "near-term," "concentrated among certain geographies." The offensive story — the new "Wingstop Smart Kitchen" back-of-house technology, tenders, the NBA partnership — dominated.
- **Third quarter 2025 (November 2025):** the crack widened. Same-store sales fell 5.6%, "below our expectations," and the softness "broaden[ed] across the industry and within our business to more geographies as well as to the middle-income consumer." Management leaned harder on three self-help levers introduced or expanded here: the Smart Kitchen (now in 2,000+ restaurants), a new "Wingstop is Here" marketing campaign, and a loyalty program, "Club Wingstop," slated for a national launch by the end of the second quarter of 2026.
- **Fourth quarter/full-year 2025 (February 2026):** the first annual same-store sales decline in 22 years (down 3% for the year). The narrative pivoted almost entirely to the three self-help initiatives and to unit growth (3,000+ restaurants surpassed, six new international markets). ## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining.** The confidence in the *long-term* vision is unwavering and consistent; confidence in the *near term* has visibly eroded, and the language has shifted from offensive to defensive-and-explanatory.

- Q1'25: "resiliency of the Wingstop brand… best story in the restaurant industry" — offensive, aspirational.
- Q3'25: "below our expectations… this dynamic broaden[ed]" — first admission of a miss, hedged with "we believe this is only temporary."
- FY'25: "first same-store sales decline in 22 years" — an acknowledgment, immediately buffered by "an impressive 35%" three-year stacked growth.
- Q1'26: "disappointing and fell below our expectations" — the most candid admission, followed immediately by external blame (weather, gas prices) and "if you exclude these unusual external factors, performance would have broadly been in line."

The tell is the growing reliance on external, non-recurring explanations and on operational metrics (speed of service, "16-point improvement," accuracy percentages) in place of the demand metric that actually matters — comparable sales, which stayed negative throughout.

**Medium, trending lower.** Management has a strong long-run delivery record — 21–22 straight years of same-store growth until 2025, and unit-development guidance that they repeatedly *raised and beat* through 2025 (a genuine, verifiable over-delivery: development guidance "jumped 100 units… almost 30% over the last 9 months," per the Q3'25 exchange). - **Low-income/Hispanic consumer exposure:** analysts pushed on this every call (Gordon Haskett, Bernstein, Stephens). Management consistently declined to quantify it ("broad strokes," "we're not overly focused"), which later proved to be the epicenter of the comp decline.
- **Value/price points:** analysts (Bank of America, Citi) probed whether Wingstop would cut price to defend traffic. - **Delivery aggregator dependence:** analysts (Bernstein, William Blair) pressed on the fact that end-to-end delivery times depend on third parties Wingstop doesn't control — an admitted gap between in-store speed gains and what the customer actually experiences.
- **Capital allocation under stress:** Bernstein directly challenged continuing buybacks versus deleveraging "in anticipation of high volatility." Management defended the buyback and conceded a drift toward ~4x leverage.

🔴 Same-store sales deteriorating four quarters straight, worst-in-22-years, with the decline *broadening* from low-income to middle-income cohorts.
🔴 Trailing earnings per share ($4.02) well below the full-year 2025 figure ($6.21), latest quarter down 67% year over year — current earnings power is contracting, not just comps.
🔴 Growing reliance on external blame (weather, gas prices) and on process metrics (speed of service) in place of demand metrics.
🔴 Negative book equity and ~$1.14B net debt while continuing aggressive buybacks into a demand downturn.
🔴 Insider signal: zero open-market buys against two open-market sells — no management conviction at these prices.

🟢 Unit development remains best-in-class: +17% unit growth in Q1'26, 3,000+ restaurants, record franchisee commitments (~2,300) — the franchise value proposition is intact and brand-partner margins actually *strengthened* in Q1'26.
🟢 The asset-light royalty model kept adjusted profit growing double digits even through an 8.7% comp decline — structural resilience.
🟢 Three concrete, now-launched self-help levers (Smart Kitchen fully deployed domestically; Club Wingstop launched; new marketing) with early proof points (Southwest region running a mid-single-digit comp premium; 10-minute-speed restaurants showing better frequency).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **Subtle reframing of the core customer.** Early calls leaned on the low-income/Hispanic base; by FY'25 and Q1'26 management is quietly re-pointing the brand at "higher-income households… earning between $50,000 and $100,000" as "the fastest-growing cohort" — an admission that the historical core is the problem cohort, dressed as strategic diversification.
- **Speed-of-service metrics substituting for comps.** The rising density of operational statistics (16-point improvement, 5-point accuracy, "raising the floor") is doing narrative work — filling the space where a positive comp number would normally sit.
- **Buyback-as-signal.** Doubling down on repurchases into negative equity and a demand air-pocket is management betting the multiple compression is overdone — but the total absence of *insider* open-market buying undercuts that signal.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: DETERIORATING (cyclically), on a still-strong structural chassis.** This is a genuinely high-quality, asset-light franchisor whose demand engine has stalled hard and whose valuation, even after a ~60% fall from its 2024 peak, is *not* cheap — roughly 38x trailing earnings and 31x free cash flow, which the peer file rightly flags as rich versus Domino's, Chipotle, Cava, Shake Shack and Portillo's. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **the "deep value / 284% margin of safety" label is a broken-model illusion.** There is no structural floor, no activist, no asset sale, no forced-selling catalyst — only a self-help operational turnaround that management promises will bend comps positive in the second half of 2026, against a low-income consumer still under real pressure. The next hard date, second-quarter 2026 earnings on July 29, 2026, is more likely a continued-negative-comp risk event than a re-rating catalyst.

**Economic moat:** intangible-brand plus scale-cost franchise economics — real, but narrow. Wings are a commodary food category with low switching costs; the moat is brand heat, marketing scale, and franchisee unit economics, not a structural lock-in. Returns are high (22.7% return on invested capital, 82.6% gross margin) and the *unit* economics are stable-to-improving, so the moat is not eroding — but the negative comps show it is not wide enough to hold demand through a consumer squeeze. **Secular threat: manageable, not terminal.** The pressure is cyclical (low-income consumer, gas prices, weather), with a secondary structural watch-item in delivery-aggregator disintermediation of the customer relationship. This is a fear-and-de-rating print on a decent business, not a melting-ice-cube — but at 38x earnings it is priced closer to the recovery than to the fear.

# Forensic Dossier — Wingstop Inc. (WING)

*Data note: the supplied transcript file is contaminated — a block of an Agios Pharmaceuticals second-quarter 2025 biotech call (thalassemia, PYRUKYND, PDUFA dates) was spliced into the middle of the Wingstop file. That material is not Wingstop's and is ignored here. This dossier rests on four genuine Wingstop calls that are present and clean: first quarter 2025 (April 30, 2025), third quarter 2025 (November 4, 2025), fourth-quarter/full-year 2025 (February 18, 2026), and first quarter 2026 (April 29, 2026).*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management tells has not changed in two years — the numbers underneath it have cracked. Across all four calls the message is identical and repeated almost word-for-word: scale toward "over 10,000 restaurants globally," drive average unit volumes (the average annual sales of a single restaurant, or "AUV") from ~$2 million toward "$3 million," and do it with an "asset-light, highly franchised model." What has changed is the ground beneath that ambition.

- **First quarter 2025 (April 2025):** the opening tone was defensive-but-confident. Same-store sales (sales at restaurants open at least a year, the cleanest read on underlying demand) rose just 0.5%, which management framed as a win against "two consecutive years of over 20%" comparisons. The consumer was flagged as soft but "near-term," "concentrated among certain geographies." The offensive story — the new "Wingstop Smart Kitchen" back-of-house technology, tenders, the NBA partnership — dominated.
- **Third quarter 2025 (November 2025):** the crack widened. Same-store sales fell 5.6%, "below our expectations," and the softness "broaden[ed] across the industry and within our business to more geographies as well as to the middle-income consumer." Management leaned harder on three self-help levers introduced or expanded here: the Smart Kitchen (now in 2,000+ restaurants), a new "Wingstop is Here" marketing campaign, and a loyalty program, "Club Wingstop," slated for a national launch by the end of the second quarter of 2026.
- **Fourth quarter/full-year 2025 (February 2026):** the first annual same-store sales decline in 22 years (down 3% for the year). The narrative pivoted almost entirely to the three self-help initiatives and to unit growth (3,000+ restaurants surpassed, six new international markets). The consumer weakness was recast as "cyclical."
- **First quarter 2026 (April 2026):** the worst print of the series — same-store sales down 8.7% — blamed on "atypical winter weather" (700+ temporary closures) and "elevated gas prices as a result of the conflict in the Middle East" hitting the low-income consumer. Full-year guidance was cut to same-store sales "down low single digits," with a promised "return to growth in the second half."

The arc, in plain terms: a beloved growth story whose comparable-sales engine has stalled hard, now betting that operational self-help (faster kitchens, loyalty, marketing) will reignite demand while unit growth keeps the system-sales and royalty machine turning.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The financial evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Best story in the restaurant industry," durable growth | Five-year revenue compounding ~25% a year (2021 $283M → 2025 $697M); earnings-per-share compounding ~45% over five years; 82.6% gross margin, 25% net margin, 22.7% return on invested capital | The *historical* quality is real and exceptional — this is a genuine premium franchisor |
| Underlying brand health "strong," weakness is "temporary/cyclical" | Same-store sales trajectory: +0.5% (Q1'25) → −5.6% (Q3'25) → −3% (FY'25) → −8.7% (Q1'26). Trailing-twelve-month earnings per share of $4.02 versus a full-year 2025 figure of $6.21, with the latest quarter's earnings per share down 67% year over year | The story is **poorer** than the recent trajectory — comps are deteriorating, not stabilizing, and current earnings power is contracting |
| Asset-light model still compounding profits | Adjusted profit (EBITDA) still grew double digits in Q1 2026; unit count +17%; system-wide sales still rising on unit growth | **Matches** — the franchise royalty machine keeps turning on new units even as same-store demand falls |
| Balance sheet supports aggressive buybacks | Net debt of ~$1.14 billion (borrowings $1.21B + leases, less $129M cash); return on equity of −16.5% is a *negative-book-equity artifact* of debt-funded buybacks, not operating losses | **Matches but flags risk** — leverage is real; management targets moving toward ~4x (from a historical 5–7x) |
| Screener "fair value $588 / 284% margin of safety" | This is a **broken-model artifact**. The Graham and Buffett fair-value outputs are mis-scaled; the same block shows a discounted-cash-flow fair value of $7.4 (equally nonsensical). At $152 the stock trades at ~38x trailing earnings and ~31x free cash flow | **Does not hold up** — do not treat this name as "deep value." The peer file correctly calls it "rich versus peers" |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining.** The confidence in the *long-term* vision is unwavering and consistent; confidence in the *near term* has visibly eroded, and the language has shifted from offensive to defensive-and-explanatory.

- Q1'25: "resiliency of the Wingstop brand… best story in the restaurant industry" — offensive, aspirational.
- Q3'25: "below our expectations… this dynamic broaden[ed]" — first admission of a miss, hedged with "we believe this is only temporary."
- FY'25: "first same-store sales decline in 22 years" — an acknowledgment, immediately buffered by "an impressive 35%" three-year stacked growth.
- Q1'26: "disappointing and fell below our expectations" — the most candid admission, followed immediately by external blame (weather, gas prices) and "if you exclude these unusual external factors, performance would have broadly been in line."

The tell is the growing reliance on external, non-recurring explanations and on operational metrics (speed of service, "16-point improvement," accuracy percentages) in place of the demand metric that actually matters — comparable sales, which stayed negative throughout.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium, trending lower.** Management has a strong long-run delivery record — 21–22 straight years of same-store growth until 2025, and unit-development guidance that they repeatedly *raised and beat* through 2025 (a genuine, verifiable over-delivery: development guidance "jumped 100 units… almost 30% over the last 9 months," per the Q3'25 exchange). But on the metric that broke — same-store sales — they have now missed their own expectations three quarters running and cut full-year guidance in Q1'26. The Q1'25 promise of a second-half "return to same-store sales growth" did not materialize; the same "return to growth in the second half" promise reappears in Q1'26. Development and profit guidance: reliable-to-sandbagged. Comparable-sales guidance: repeatedly optimistic and repeatedly wrong through this downturn.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Low-income/Hispanic consumer exposure:** analysts pushed on this every call (Gordon Haskett, Bernstein, Stephens). Management consistently declined to quantify it ("broad strokes," "we're not overly focused"), which later proved to be the epicenter of the comp decline.
- **Value/price points:** analysts (Bank of America, Citi) probed whether Wingstop would cut price to defend traffic. Management repeatedly refused ("training a guest to come to you for a $3 menu item… is not who Wingstop is"), a defensible brand stance but one that leaves comps exposed if the value-seeking consumer doesn't return.
- **Delivery aggregator dependence:** analysts (Bernstein, William Blair) pressed on the fact that end-to-end delivery times depend on third parties Wingstop doesn't control — an admitted gap between in-store speed gains and what the customer actually experiences.
- **Capital allocation under stress:** Bernstein directly challenged continuing buybacks versus deleveraging "in anticipation of high volatility." Management defended the buyback and conceded a drift toward ~4x leverage.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 Same-store sales deteriorating four quarters straight, worst-in-22-years, with the decline *broadening* from low-income to middle-income cohorts.
🔴 Trailing earnings per share ($4.02) well below the full-year 2025 figure ($6.21), latest quarter down 67% year over year — current earnings power is contracting, not just comps.
🔴 Growing reliance on external blame (weather, gas prices) and on process metrics (speed of service) in place of demand metrics.
🔴 Negative book equity and ~$1.14B net debt while continuing aggressive buybacks into a demand downturn.
🔴 Insider signal: zero open-market buys against two open-market sells — no management conviction at these prices.

🟢 Unit development remains best-in-class: +17% unit growth in Q1'26, 3,000+ restaurants, record franchisee commitments (~2,300) — the franchise value proposition is intact and brand-partner margins actually *strengthened* in Q1'26.
🟢 The asset-light royalty model kept adjusted profit growing double digits even through an 8.7% comp decline — structural resilience.
🟢 Three concrete, now-launched self-help levers (Smart Kitchen fully deployed domestically; Club Wingstop launched; new marketing) with early proof points (Southwest region running a mid-single-digit comp premium; 10-minute-speed restaurants showing better frequency).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **Subtle reframing of the core customer.** Early calls leaned on the low-income/Hispanic base; by FY'25 and Q1'26 management is quietly re-pointing the brand at "higher-income households… earning between $50,000 and $100,000" as "the fastest-growing cohort" — an admission that the historical core is the problem cohort, dressed as strategic diversification.
- **Speed-of-service metrics substituting for comps.** The rising density of operational statistics (16-point improvement, 5-point accuracy, "raising the floor") is doing narrative work — filling the space where a positive comp number would normally sit.
- **Buyback-as-signal.** Doubling down on repurchases into negative equity and a demand air-pocket is management betting the multiple compression is overdone — but the total absence of *insider* open-market buying undercuts that signal.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: DETERIORATING (cyclically), on a still-strong structural chassis.** This is a genuinely high-quality, asset-light franchisor whose demand engine has stalled hard and whose valuation, even after a ~60% fall from its 2024 peak, is *not* cheap — roughly 38x trailing earnings and 31x free cash flow, which the peer file rightly flags as rich versus Domino's, Chipotle, Cava, Shake Shack and Portillo's. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **the "deep value / 284% margin of safety" label is a broken-model illusion.** There is no structural floor, no activist, no asset sale, no forced-selling catalyst — only a self-help operational turnaround that management promises will bend comps positive in the second half of 2026, against a low-income consumer still under real pressure. The next hard date, second-quarter 2026 earnings on July 29, 2026, is more likely a continued-negative-comp risk event than a re-rating catalyst.

**Economic moat:** intangible-brand plus scale-cost franchise economics — real, but narrow. Wings are a commodary food category with low switching costs; the moat is brand heat, marketing scale, and franchisee unit economics, not a structural lock-in. Returns are high (22.7% return on invested capital, 82.6% gross margin) and the *unit* economics are stable-to-improving, so the moat is not eroding — but the negative comps show it is not wide enough to hold demand through a consumer squeeze. **Secular threat: manageable, not terminal.** The pressure is cyclical (low-income consumer, gas prices, weather), with a secondary structural watch-item in delivery-aggregator disintermediation of the customer relationship. This is a fear-and-de-rating print on a decent business, not a melting-ice-cube — but at 38x earnings it is priced closer to the recovery than to the fear.
